newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end sharply up on foreign limit rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end sharply up on foreign limit rise.

text.p: A rush to buy blue-chip shares ahead of next month's expansion of the foreign shareholding limit boosted the South Korean stock market on Wednesday, brokers said.
The composite index provisionally ended up 21.84 points, or 2.84 percent, to 791.64, on heavy volume.
The foreign shareholding ceiling will be raised to 20 percent for most stocks from October 1, above the current 18 percent limit, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
Trading was active, with 28.58 million shares changing hands. On Tuesday, volume was a thin 16.38 million.
"The shares that hit their upper limits today were all domestic consumption-related stocks like telecommunications, utilities and city banks," said Shinyoung Securities analsyt Steven Lee.
KEPCO led the market's rise, soaring 1,400 won to its limit high of 25,800.
Korea Mobile Telecom jumped 32,000 won to its limit of 577,000. SEOULBANK was the most active stock of the day, rising 210 won to 5,390.
Brokers said investors were too focused on the rise in the foreign investment ceiling to worry about hostilities in Iraq.
"But if the situation goes on much longer, investors will start realising higher oil prices would hurt the economy and impact the market," a Daewoo Research Institute analyst said.
The United States has launched missile attacks on Iraq over the past two days. South Korea imports most of its crude oil from the Middle East.
Shinyoung's Lee said the index could test 800 on Thursday, but would face selling pressure.
"This is a short-term bounce that will be hard to maintain because the economic fundamentals haven't changed and the supply and demand situation hasn't improved," said a local broker.

An overhang of margin loans that must be repaid this month is looming over the market. As of August 31, margin loans at brokerage houses reached 2.61 trillion won, while customer deposits lagged at 2.35 trillion.
Four firms will hold initial public offerings on Thursday.

Hyundai Housing will offer 6.2 million shares at 14,000 won per share, AUK Corp 469,000 shares at 16,000 won, Dong Yang Elevator 600,000 shares at 22,000 won, and Korea Electronic Terminal 280,000 shares at 36,000 won.
The September futures contract rose 2.15 points to 85.20, while the KOSPI 200 index gained 2.33 points to 84.77.
